note: Regression fixtures proposed to the fixtures layer. Each one restates a defect recorded in data/field-reports as a scenario with an observable expectation. `sources` are <library id>#<issue number>; stats.mjs fails if one is not in the data.

fixtures.scenario: Popup with placement inline-end/start under dir=rtl opens on the physical left and aligns to the trigger's right edge; physical `left`/`right` placements are not mirrored.
Anchor near each viewport edge in RTL: the popup flips to whichever physical side has room and stays inside the viewport.
For every placement × direction the popup arrow is rendered, centred on the anchor and points at it.
RTL document with a classic scrollbar on the left, absolute and fixed strategies: popup inline edge equals anchor inline edge (no offset by scrollbar width).
Popup shown in the top layer (native popover/dialog), direction switched at runtime: position stays correct.
RTL nested menu: submenu opens toward the left, its chevron points left, ArrowLeft opens it and ArrowRight closes it.
Trigger inside a dir=rtl container in an LTR document: dialog, popover, menu, tooltip and toast content rendered in a portal has dir=rtl and RTL layout.
Only <html dir=rtl>, no provider: tabs, slider, menu, scroll area behave and render RTL, and no component writes dir=ltr on itself.
An LTR island inside an RTL page and an RTL island inside an LTR page render correctly; toggling direction on a mounted tree equals a fresh mount.
Locale ar with direction forced to ltr (and locale en with direction rtl): layout and keys follow the explicit direction, strings and numerals follow the locale.
RTL slider: minimum at the right; pointer at 25% from the right edge gives 25%; ArrowLeft increases, Home goes to minimum; marks sit at their values.
Slider, progress, switch and rating accept direction=ltr inside an RTL page (media timeline) without changing locale.
Switch in RTL: checked thumb at inline-end (left), thumb rect inside track rect in both states, also after a live direction change.
Determinate, buffer and indeterminate progress fill and travel from right to left in RTL; the striped/active animation runs the same way.
Rating 3.5 in RTL fills the right half of the fourth star; hovering the right half of a star selects the half value.
RTL carousel: all slides render, next moves content so that the following slide enters from the left, the next button is on the left and points left, dots follow the same order.
Roving focus for (horizontal, vertical, both) × (ltr, rtl): left/right swap only in RTL, up/down never; Home/End follow the same mapping.
Data grid and calendar grid in RTL: ArrowLeft moves focus to the cell visually on the left.
Tree in RTL: ArrowLeft expands a collapsed node, ArrowRight collapses it; indentation and toggle are at inline-start.
Chart with a reversed category axis in RTL: ArrowLeft focuses the next data point.
Back/forward, chevron and previous/next icons mirror in RTL; clocks, checkmarks, media controls and spinners do not; icons with a named counterpart swap to it.
Pagination, calendar header and image preview in RTL: previous is at inline-start pointing right, next at inline-end pointing left, and labels match actions.
Custom start/end icons passed through slots are used in RTL as in LTR.
One scroll adapter: in RTL, scrolling to inline-end and back reports 0…max in every engine; tab scroll buttons, header/body sync and aligned containers use it.
Virtualised grid in RTL: at every horizontal offset (including both ends, and combined with vertical/infinite scrolling) the rendered column range covers the viewport.
Grid with start- and end-pinned columns in RTL: pinned cells stay at their edges while scrolling, are opaque, nothing is clipped, shadows are on the scrolled side, sticky rows compose.
Column pinned to `start` is on the right in RTL; a physical `left` (if accepted) is on the left in both directions.
RTL table: dragging a column's inline-end handle outward widens it; keyboard resize follows visual direction.
Opening a modal on an RTL page with a classic scrollbar (on the left) shifts neither body content nor fixed elements.
RTL page with every form control and an open popup: document scrollWidth equals clientWidth (no overflow from visually hidden inputs or focus guards).
A dir=ltr email/phone/password/number field inside an RTL form: its text is LTR and its adornments, label notch, padding and radii are consistent with the field's own direction.
RTL fields with start/end adornments, clear button, feedback icon and select indicator: none overlaps the text, widths do not change while typing.
OTP/PIN input under dir=rtl: the first typed digit lands in the leftmost slot and slots read left to right.
Animated badge counter 10 and 125 in RTL read 10 and 125; a hh:mm toolbar reads hours then minutes.
`1–5 of 5`, `2 / 10` and `21–30 of 100` inside an RTL paragraph, with Latin and with Arabic words, keep each number and range intact and in order.
Date and time fields for ar, he and fa: segment visual order equals the locale's formatted string, for slash, dash, dot and space patterns.
Formatted dates and field values contain no bidi control characters; parsing accepts and ignores them; shipped bundles contain none as literals.
Typing 123, ١٢٣ and ۱۲۳ into number and date fields yields 123; the display numbering system stays the configured one.
parse(format(x)) = x for every CLDR locale × numbering system; punctuation-only or whitespace-only input never changes the numbering system.
Date field with arab and arabext digits: no NaN in any segment, stepping a segment keeps the value valid, for Gregorian, Hijri and Persian calendars.
Formatting a date for ar with numbering system arab and with latn changes every numeric field and nothing else; predicates do not depend on digits.
Arabic day period: 00:00 and 11:59 give ص, 12:00 and 23:59 give م, in every Arabic regional locale.
Every Umm al-Qura month in the supported range has 29 or 30 days, years have 354 or 355, and conversion agrees with ICU islamic-umalqura day by day.
Persian calendar: Esfand 1403 has 30 days, every month of 1403–1405 starts on day 1, Gregorian↔Persian round-trips over several centuries, old years render with any time zone.
Full, medium and short dates and every caption layout in Hijri and Persian calendars draw day, month name and year from that calendar (no Gregorian day or month).
Hijri calendar: from the 30th of a month, next month lands in the following month (clamped), never skipping one.
Weekday headers for ar, he and fa use CLDR narrow/short forms, are distinct, fit the cell, and match the column order of the day cells.
Day cells with latn, arab and arabext digits are optically centred in each bundled font.
A Hijri date formats in English with Latin digits and in Arabic with either digit set; importing calendar support changes no global state.

Chart in RTL: value axis at the right, tick labels outside the plot, legend marks before labels, continuous legend reversed with its labels, tooltip box padding correct, highlights on the data points, legend click toggles the clicked series.
Tabs and segmented control in RTL, including overflow and a direction change: after the transition the indicator rect equals the selected item's rect; it starts from the right.
Drawer on start, end, left and right in RTL: placed on the resolved side, first animation frame adjacent to that edge, resize handle on the inner edge, close button at inline-end.
Toast region at `end` is on the left in RTL and swipe-to-dismiss goes toward that edge; a physical `right` stays right.
Lint over recipes, examples and docs: no physical inline property or class (left/right margins, paddings, insets, radii, text-align) outside the listed physical-geometry exemptions.
Stack/group with spacing and with dividers in RTL: equal gaps between all items, none at the edges, dividers between items.
Attached button group, split button and date range ends in RTL: outer corners rounded, inner square, divider between.
Absolutely centred child and slider mark labels are centred in RTL.
Vertically oriented splitter, slider, tabs and steps render identically along the block axis in LTR and RTL.
Content inside dir=auto that resolves to RTL gets RTL styles and behaviour.
Build check: every message key of every component (visible and aria) has an Arabic value; base `ar` exists without a region.
CSV export of Arabic cell text opens correctly in Excel (UTF-8 with BOM), compared byte for byte.
